temporal_edit_router.role: Inference-time VLM temporal-edit classifier, not merely an offline evaluator; do not train a VLM as the first step.
temporal_edit_router.question: Does the requested edit require changing the source temporal structure? This is a prediction, not a guarantee about the generated output.
temporal_edit_router.no_temporal_edit: Use fixed corresponding-frame target_i -> source_i sparsity, subject to validating the temporal-alignment premise.
temporal_edit_router.temporal_edit: Use a limited full-attention probe to estimate target-source correspondence, then use correspondence-guided sparsity.
undecided_details: VLM model and calibrated uncertainty policy; no external inference API has been selected or invoked.
Probe layers/heads/denoising steps, confidence checks, refresh schedule, and fallback when correspondence is unreliable.
Full-attention probabilities are not automatically available from fused attention; avoid materializing the entire quadratic matrix.
Handle insertions, deletions, repeated actions, and many-to-many or missing correspondence; do not force every target frame to one source frame.
temporal_edit_router.ablation: Preserve A/B/C definitions; test the router as a separate C+ extension so gains are not confounded with fixed-frame sparsity.
temporal_edit_router.timing: Include classifier, full-attention probe, correspondence construction, and fallback costs in system end-to-end latency. Offline evaluation cost remains separate.
temporal_edit_router.quality_check: Compare source and generated outputs offline to validate actual temporal behavior; pre-generation classification cannot prove preservation.

fair_comparison_requirements: Match physical card count, parallelism, dtype, offload, source preprocessing, output shape, seed, scheduler, and measured NFE.
Keep the original VDN linear update in this stage; do not introduce linear simplification or few-step distillation.
Report DiT latency, end-to-end latency, memory, editing fidelity, retained content, and temporal consistency separately.
Do not compare old 8-card Ref2VA logs to a new single-card VDN result as an acceleration ratio.
Do not extrapolate five-block random-input timings into measured complete-video performance.
